supersedes: reports/c58_residue_partition.json in full. All three of its readings were proxies for the matcher's decision. This is the decision itself.
how: evaluate_boundary_strict already records WHY it rejected each branch, in the miss text. No instrumentation was needed -- I had been carrying the answer in branch_misses the whole time and building HP and decomposition proxies alongside it.
what_this_says: The residue is not a mixture of unrelated shapes. 93% of it dies at ONE check: roll_component_events_agree, the comparison that decides whether a roll-dependent magnitude is consistent with the legal roll set. Only 23 rows are rejected by the exact-component check on their majority arm.
why_this_beats_every_partition_i_publish: The three earlier readings -- 183/107/50, 132/53/50, 17/265/58 -- all asked a question I invented ('does some branch reproduce the observation, by a rule I chose') and then treated the answer as a bucketing. The matcher does not use my rule. This reports the check that actually fired, so it cannot disagree with the gate it is meant to explain.
the_next_question_is_now_specific: Within roll_component_events_agree, which sub-condition rejects these 318? The candidates are the legal-roll-set derivation, the branch-local support, the cap/_to_full relaxation, and the component pairing. That is a bounded set inside one function rather than a search across the whole residue.
lesson_recorded_because_it_cost_three_cy: When the goal is to explain a gate's verdict, instrument the gate. I built three proxies for a decision whose reasons were already serialised on every row. Controls did not catch it because the proxies were consistently wrong, not randomly wrong -- a control tells you whether two populations differ under YOUR test, not whether your test is the right one.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 341
